draft.title: Conventions of drama
card: a speech in which a character is alone on stage and speaks their thoughts aloud. The audience hears what the character really thinks or fears.
a short remark a character speaks to the audience, or to themselves, while other characters are on stage. The others are meant not to hear it.
notes in the script, often in italics or brackets, that guide how the play is performed. They can describe movement, tone, lighting, sound or the setting.
These conventions help a playwright show what a character thinks and feels. Dialogue alone cannot always do that.
draft.remember: Soliloquy: alone, thoughts aloud. Aside: heard by the audience only. Stage directions: guide the performance.

a.q: Alone on stage, Dev says aloud that he is afraid to tell his father the truth. What is this?
a.why: Dev is alone and speaks his private thoughts aloud, so this is a soliloquy. It is not an aside, because an aside is a short remark made while other characters are present.
a.clue: Is anyone else on stage with Dev?

b.q: In a scene, Mia chats with her boss, then turns to the audience and mutters that she dislikes him. He does not hear her. What is this?
b.why: Mia speaks to the audience while another character is on stage, and he does not hear her. That is an aside. It is not a soliloquy, because she is not alone on stage.
b.clue: Check whether Mia is alone when she speaks.
